title: MoonBoot process
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/70618960fe794f7cb6460757a168f378MOONBOOT_thumbnail.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/1fe25ed2fde44d7987b2888004378ec1MOONBOOT_thumbnail.png)

* * *

**Creating the MOON Boot**

I created the MOON Boot completely from scratch in CLO3D, using references and photographs as a guide. The process took some time, as not everything worked perfectly on the first try.

At the time I was working on this project, the Lacing Tool had not yet been updated, so I created the laces in Houdini using splines.

Once the model was finished, I prepared the UVs and exported it as an FBX file to 3ds Max. There, I did some additional optimization and reworked the UV layout to make the model more convenient to texture later in Substance Painter.

I textured the model entirely in Substance Painter. Once the textures were finished and I was happy with the result, I started building the rendering scene in Houdini using Karma.

For the lighting setup, I use an HDRI with a Dome Light, combined with several Area Lights to create the specific atmosphere and mood I want. Then, I set up the materials using the textures I created in Substance Painter.

Finally, I set up the camera and created a turntable render.![71263221ab104ac2a45f01dc05ba23e8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/71263221ab104ac2a45f01dc05ba23e8MOONBOOT_thumbnail.png)![0dcd9a76ece14d509f235883c50b129c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/0dcd9a76ece14d509f235883c50b129cMOONBOOT_thumbnail_2.png)![dfe082bf260c4165b0333d2f6ff1b407](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/dfe082bf260c4165b0333d2f6ff1b40711111.png)![90817afe4cd44a89be78f15ab1a39e71](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/38602b6476464d4288d3fc32d5e3f904/images/90817afe4cd44a89be78f15ab1a39e71MOONBOOT_thumbnail.jpg)

title: 2D CLO patterns - nesting - DXF - cutter
content:
Hi everyone,

Is there anyone here who sends their created and graded patterns from CLO3D in DXF format directly to a cutter after nesting?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: For production use, I’d first make sure the exported DXF preserves the correct scale, grading, notches, seam information, and pattern-piece labels before sending it to the cutter.It’s also a good idea to open the DXF in the receiving nesting or cutting software and verify a few known measurements against the original CLO pattern. That can help catch scaling or export-setting issues before fabric is cut.For graded patterns, I’d also confirm that every size is included correctly and that the nesting system recognizes all pattern outlines as expected.
content_description: This page serves to connect CLO3D users seeking advice on sending nested, graded DXF patterns directly to cutters.

title: Pit Stop to Pattern Pieces: How an Indian Fashion Student Brought F1 to the Digital Runway
content:
## _Most F1 fans stop at the merch store. Sanjivani Rana went further, translating the engineering-driven aesthetics of six Formula 1 teams into a 12-look CLO collection built on color theory, garment ergonomics, and modular construction. We sat down with her to find out how a fashion student turns racewear technology into something you'd actually want to wear._

* * *

![6ccc6a6f40c84960ad83990f34f177e1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202607/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/6ccc6a6f40c84960ad83990f34f177e1%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202026-07-30%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%92%E1%85%AE%205.01.49.png)![44b856e160684a2c874ed7c086546f0c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202607/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/44b856e160684a2c874ed7c086546f0c%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202026-07-30%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%92%E1%85%AE%205.02.15.png)

**Q: Could you briefly introduce yourself and share a little bit about your background?**

Hi, I'm Sanjivani Rana, a fashion design student based in India who recently completed her bachelor's degree. I thrive on creative exploration and hands-on experimentation. I don't confine myself to a single style or medium. I'm a proud jack of all trades, constantly learning, evolving, and discovering new ways to express ideas. Lately, I've been deep into digital design, especially CLO, where I get to merge fashion-forward concepts with technology.

**Q: What sparked your interest in 3D fashion, and how did you transition from traditional to digital design?**

Semester 7 was the turning point. I was introduced to 3D design through one of my modules, and it completely changed how I thought about fashion. The transition from traditional to digital wasn't overnight. It started with basic garment sketches, but once I got comfortable with CLO, I realized I could visualize designs faster, adjust patterns in real time, and experiment without waste. That shift gave me so much more freedom to iterate. It also made me see how digital fashion could break boundaries, not just in design but in production and sustainability too.

**Q: Where does your passion for Formula 1 come from, and how does it influence your creative work?**

It started with Netflix's "Drive to Survive." I was completely hooked from the first episode and binge-watched everything. The more I followed the sport, the more I became captivated by the precision, speed, and dedication behind each team. How a single turn can define a team's entire season. So when I got an assignment to create a collection of 12 pieces, Formula 1 was the only answer. I crafted two outfits for each of six teams: Ferrari, Red Bull, McLaren, Mercedes AMG Petronas, Williams Racing, and Aston Martin, letting their distinct identities and aesthetics come to life through the designs.

![e4a5cf832e734897bfbf514067e84e29](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/e4a5cf832e734897bfbf514067e84e29%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202026-08-06%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%8C%E1%85%A5%E1%86%AB%209.38.08.png)![6b185eb747cb43d39d97a3219018240c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/6b185eb747cb43d39d97a3219018240cimage.png)![a273ab1657704a0a9a5dda521b071454](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/a273ab1657704a0a9a5dda521b071454image.png)

**Q: Your F1 Runway project feels like engineering brought into fashion. What inspired this concept?**

After getting into F1, I started noticing how much merchandise was out there, and it was almost always just oversized jerseys or basic vests. That gap sparked something in me. If I was going to use F1 as a theme, I had to push further. I wanted pieces that actually embodied the energy, precision, and innovation of the sport. Fashion-forward, not just fan pieces.

**Q: How did you approach turning the mechanical aesthetics of race cars into wearable designs while staying true to each team's identity?**

I started by dissecting what makes each team visually distinct: the aerodynamic lines, modular structures, color systems. Then I translated those elements into silhouettes and tailoring. The designs aren't overly technical, but each look is built so that at a glance, you know exactly which team it belongs to. Color choices, graphic details, the overall energy. I wanted the team identity to be unmistakable even without needing to read a label.

![af9066f2d3a34846a58c6464cf064482](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202607/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/af9066f2d3a34846a58c6464cf0644821.png)![abf7eafbc92744ff9315ab881d973180](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202607/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/abf7eafbc92744ff9315ab881d9731802.png)

**Q: You've spoken about how digital fashion can outpace traditional methods. How did that show up in your CLO workflow?**

The biggest difference was not needing physical samples. I could iterate on fits, adjust patterns, and fine-tune details digitally without any material waste. CLO's simulation also let me see exactly how the fabric would drape and move on the body before committing to anything. That level of realism meant I could move faster without guessing. Every seam, every drape was exactly as I envisioned it.

**Q: You mentioned your mentor was like a "pit crew" during this process. How did their guidance help?**

Just like a driver needs a pit crew to get back on track after a rough patch, she was there at every step. Whenever I hit a creative wall or needed a fresh perspective, her guidance was steady. She wasn't just a mentor. She was a real partner in the process: always kind, always present, always helping me fine-tune the details. Like a pit crew pushing a driver toward their best lap.

**Q: Young GenZ designers in India are moving beyond traditional styles and experimenting with global concepts like sportswear or gaming-inspired designs. Have you seen that shift?**

Definitely. The silhouettes coming out of young designers in India right now are bold, dramatic, almost futuristic. Sculptural, daring, avatar-like. It doesn't feel like fashion following a trend anymore. It feels like a whole new era taking shape. And I think we're just at the beginning of it.  


![f1953a57e21d4692bb7338ec50e1535d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202607/8a9d32c9ff184b5a8466837640b610c7/images/f1953a57e21d4692bb7338ec50e1535d%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3%E1%84%8F%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AB%E1%84%89%E1%85%A3%E1%86%BA%202026-07-30%20%E1%84%8B%E1%85%A9%E1%84%92%E1%85%AE%205.22.12.png)

**Q: Looking ahead, what direction do you see your career in digital fashion taking? And what would you say to students just starting out with CLO?**

I want to keep moving toward more immersive, concept-driven work where fashion and technology genuinely coexist. I'm especially drawn to collections that feel emotionally impactful and still functional. CLO is a big part of that vision.

For students starting out: the technical side is less scary than it looks. The more you experiment, the more the software becomes a natural part of how you think. Treat it as a tool for your imagination, not a wall between you and your ideas. Be patient, stay curious, and let the mistakes teach you. Digital fashion is moving fast, and this is a genuinely exciting time to be in it.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Great interview and an inspiring project. I really like the focus on using CLO3D to iterate quickly while maintaining strong design intent. Translating technical inspiration like Formula 1 into wearable fashion takes both creativity and a solid understanding of garment construction. Wishing Sanjivani all the best in her digital fashion journey!
content_description: Showcasing how fashion student Sanjivani Rana transforms Formula 1 team aesthetics into innovative, digitally designed garments that blend engineering precision with wearable style through 3D fashion technology.

title: Erreur Export VRM
content:
Bonjour j'essai de créé des vêtement personnalisé pour des VRM que je crée et que j'import sur clo3D nu, une fois le vêtement réalisé, lorsque j'exporte mon fichier VRM, le fichier est corrompu il ne s'ouvre dans auccun logiciel qui acceptent des fichier VRM même quand je teste mon fichier vrm issu de clo3d sur ce site [https://vrm-viewer.ownverse.world/ ](https://vrm-viewer.ownverse.world/) il y a quand même l'erreur. Je ne comprends pas pourquoi je ne peux pas simplement importer / habiller et Exporter mon VRM avec Clo3D et Utiliser après mon fichier VRM ailleurs. Quelqu'un a rencontré ce type de problème ? peut-être que je m'y prends mal ? je n'ai pas envie de convertir mon VRM pour VRchat, je veux l'utiliser tel quel, même si le fichier comporte une Erreur en l'ouvrant dans un logiciel qui acceptent les fichier VRM, si j'ouvre mon fichier Vrm problématique dans Blender, on peut voir le personnage + le vêtement créé, mais moi je n'ai aucune idée de comment utiliser Blender dans ce cas. D'ailleurs pourquoi si j'ai un logiciel fort comme clo3D je suis obligé d'avoir constament blender pour X tache ?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, n'hésite pas également à contacter le support technique en joignant ton fichier https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/5a35e3b2f21c42c8a884cec213b51b4d - Comme c'est un logiciel externe, il est possible qu'on mette un peu de temps à te répondre. Note aussi que la réponse sera en anglais car l'équipe support ne parle pas français. :)
Reply 1: d'accord je vais envoyé un compte rendu sur les défaut rencontré avec l'export vrm simple et celui de everywear pour vrchat, dans l'ensemble j'ai pu régler le problème avec l'export VRM dans Everywear de Vrchat : mes UV pour l'avatar était supperposé aux UV du vêtement, et oui il faut passer par Blender pour corriger le VRM (les couleurs même si y a l'ajout dans clo3d du toon shader ça ne fonctionne pas bien, les cartes UV exporté avec l'export VRM de EveryWear ne sont pas bon non plus, j'ai du faire un export des UV Map (Avatar et Vêtement) depuis l'éditeur UV dans clo3d pour avoir les bon rendu dans blender grace à l'add on VRM). Le bon point sur l'export VRM pour VRCHAT depuis Everywear c'est que le vêtement reste attaché sur l'avatar contrairement à l'export VRM simple ou le vêtement reste figé alors que l'avatar bouge... j'espère que ça pourra aider les autres qui rencontre le même problème, Bonne journée chez-vous 🙂❤️

Comment 2: Je pense que le problème vient du fait que CLO3D n'est pas un éditeur VRM complet. Bien qu'il permette d'importer et d'exporter des maillages, il ne conserve pas toujours toutes les données spécifiques au format VRM (métadonnées, *spring bones*, expressions, paramètres du squelette humanoïde, etc.) ; il peut en résulter un fichier VRM qui s'ouvre dans Blender mais échoue à la validation dans les visionneuses VRM.Une méthode plus fiable consiste à utiliser CLO3D pour créer le vêtement, à l'exporter au format FBX ou OBJ, puis à l'intégrer à votre VRM d'origine dans Blender à l'aide de l'add-on VRM. De cette façon, vous préservez l'intégrité des données VRM initiales tout en remplaçant ou en ajoutant uniquement le vêtement.Par curiosité, quelle version de CLO3D utilisez-vous ? Je sais que la prise en charge du format VRM a évolué au fil des versions.
Reply 1: coucou merci pour ta réponse, j'utilise la dernière version de clo3D celle conçu justement pour l'import export vrm... je vais suivre tes conseils en exportant uniquement le modèle en fbx, j'ai vu hier également que l'export fbx du modèle et de l'avatar fonctionnais si j'utilisais everywear (export général pas vrchat) j"utiliserai blender et l'add on VRM pour convertir mon fbx en VRM, j'espère que dans le future clo3d améliora cette fonctionnalité, Bonne journée Poshyi 🙂
content_description: Cette page vise à partager et résoudre les problèmes liés à l'importation, la personnalisation et l'exportation de fichiers VRM avec Clo3D, en particulier concernant les erreurs de corruption empêchant leur utilisation dans d'autres logiciels sans conversion.

title: Pattern with All-Over Graphic Rendering as Transparent?
content:
![c5bdc56d9a5b457fbd463e246195b829](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/f475cb7a12ce40d5952747fe591be371/images/c5bdc56d9a5b457fbd463e246195b829Outfit1Posed_Custom_View_1_1.png)![92f280f312994c04b675abba13e92642](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/f475cb7a12ce40d5952747fe591be371/images/92f280f312994c04b675abba13e92642Screenshot%202026-08-03%20at%204.35.13%E2%80%AFPM.png)

Hi! I'm using CLO version 2026.0.374 to try to render this skirt I created. The front right panel has an all-over graphic on it, while the front left panel has graphics on the bottom.

Both sets of graphics look fine in the 3D window, but when I render it, the graphics look transparent and pixelly.

Both sets of graphics are transparent PNGs that are at 100% opacity, and are set to blend with the base fabric.

I've already tried toggling the render shadow per other community posts running into the same issue, but to no avail. I wanted to see if there was a workaround for this that doesn't involve installing an older version of CLO. Any ideas?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I forgot to add: This seems to only be happening in the final render. The skirt and graphics look perfectly fine in the interactive render.
Reply 1: Hi, can you check the Z-Offset of all graphics involved and see if they are overlapping with something? Is there a Displacement Map on the fabrics that could be overlaying with them?
Reply 2: Hi, sorry for the late response but doubling the z-offset of each graphic definitely helped! Thank you so much!
Reply 3: Hi, great to hear that was the fix! ❤️
content_description: A community support page seeking solutions for rendering transparent PNG graphics correctly on skirt panels in CLO 2026 without reverting to older software versions.
